idiom_name: Vitest/Jest typed module mock (vi.mock + vi.mocked) over the service module
implementation_notes: TypeScript's contribution is that the stand-in can be checked against the contract: vi.mock replaces the service module and vi.mocked(price) gives the fake the real signatures, so deleting or renaming an operation breaks the test at compile time; a plain object annotated with the service interface does the same without a framework. When the wire format matters, MSW's typed handlers intercept at the network layer and the real client code runs against declared responses. Use the module mock for client logic and the network-level handler for serialization, status handling and retries.
pitfalls: A cast (as any, as PriceService) destroys the only advantage TypeScript gives here: with a cast the fake keeps compiling after the contract changed, which is precisely the drift a typed stand-in prevents.
vi.mock is hoisted above the imports and its factory cannot close over top-level variables, so shared fixtures must come from vi.hoisted or a __mocks__ module.
Structural typing lets an incomplete object pass when the target type is inferred rather than annotated, so annotate the stand-in with the interface instead of relying on inference.

variants.name: Structural fake annotated with the service interface
variants.implementation_notes: With structural typing a plain object can be the stand-in, and the annotating type or the satisfies operator makes the compiler reject an object that no longer matches the contract - the same guarantee a mocking library provides, without the library or its hoisting rules. Use it for hand-written doubles with real canned behaviour and for reuse outside tests.
pitfalls: satisfies checks the object literal but does not widen it, so later property access stays narrow - helpful for assertions, confusing if the fake is expected to be replaceable at runtime.
Optional or overloaded members let an incomplete object satisfy the interface; keep the service interface narrow enough that a missing operation is a compile error.

variants.name: MSW typed request handlers (network-level stand-in)
variants.idiom_name: setupServer(http.get(...) -> HttpResponse.json(...)) with typed path params
variants.implementation_notes: MSW replaces the service at the network layer, so the production client, its serialization and its status handling all run: handlers are declared as route plus response and work in Node, the browser and a development mode. Typed path parameters and response bodies keep the handlers in step with the API description, which is where the type safety lives once the seam moves from the module to the wire.
pitfalls: Handlers are typed by hand unless the project derives them from an OpenAPI document or a type-safe helper, so the wire contract can still drift from the code.
The same handler set used for development and tests means an accidental production-enabling of the mock runtime is a real risk: keep the browser worker registration out of production builds.
